thread:
emma: posted an RFC draft for a lightweight on-prem upgrade handshake that tries to avoid sidecars and operator surprise. core idea: a tiny immutable boot image (turnstile) pulls component bundles, emits an attestable receipt per-bundle, and only flips a dataset/component "activated" bit after operator-validated receipts or an automatic policy window. please skim — looking for gaps around partial fetch, GC, and operator UX. link: https://rwd-internal/notes/rfc/component-turnstile (draft)
.tomas: skimmed it. promising. how do we handle a node that successfully fetches bundle A but times out on bundle B? do we block app traffic until all bundles active?
.li-chen: i think we should differentiate: critical vs best-effort bundles. critical bundles block activation; best-effort can go into degraded mode with feature flags. receipts should include bundle role.
.jonah: question on receipts: are they signed only by the node, or by the node+verifier once verified? ordering matters for rollbacks.
.emma: receipts are node-signed + boot-image-signed metadata. the verifier (operator control plane) can append a verification attestation. rough example in RFC:
```json
{
  "node_id": "node-42",
  "boot_version": "1.2.0",
  "bundles": [
    {"name":"model-core","sha256":"abc123...","size":123456789,"role":"critical","status":"fetched"},
    {"name":"lang-pack-en","sha256":"def456...","size":23456,"role":"best-effort","status":"partial"}
  ],
  "timestamp": "2026-02-12T18:00:00Z",
  "signature": "---base64-node-sig---"
}
```
.emma: flow: turnstile pulls -> writes receipt -> attempts activation policy -> if all critical bundles present, flips local state and reports. operator can hit /v1/operator/nodes/{id}/inspect to view receipts and /accept to force activation.
.tomas: OK. operator acceptance API needs an audit reason and optional snapshot of receipts returned. also we need a safe-mode where node serves only control-plane APIs until operator resolves — otherwise, silent partial activations will break customers.
.li-chen: implementation note: receipts should be compact and compressible. keep a separate rolling index file rather than storing full receipts forever. propose: keep last N receipts + aggregated merkle root for history. also TTL + compress before sending to control plane.
.jonah: storage/GC: nodes will churn; receipts for older versions can be pruned after X days. but we must keep enough for postmortem (configurable retention per-customer). add a GC policy doc 👍
.deploy-bot: emma pinned the RFC draft in #architecture and scheduled a short sync on Tue 10:30 PT. :calendar:
.emma: action items i'll track:
- li-chen: add CLI/UX mock for operator inspect/accept (include audit text + snapshot)
- jonah: sketch GC/retention policy + compression options
- tomas: write verifier API spec (endpoints + auth + failure semantics)
- emma: update RFC with explicit critical vs best-effort roles and sample state machine
.tomas: quick nit — call the boot image "turnstile" in docs but use a more neutral name in APIs (eg: bootstrap-agent) so legal/docs folks don't choke.
.li-chen: noted. will include both names and a glossary entry.
.jonah: i'll drop a strawman GC policy into the RFC tomorrow. also adding a simulation note: what if 30% of nodes report partial bundles after a release? fallback: automatic rollback window (48h) + operator alert.
.emma: thanks — this is helpful. expect a revised draft by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
.tomas: ack. :eyes:
.li-chen: ack. :white_check_mark:
.jonah: ack, will follow up with GC draft.
